quote:
Participating in the Womate She Leads Programme has been a valuable learning experience for me. The 5 weeks sessions has taught me a lot of things.
The programme provided an opportunity to improve my knowledge of climate change, environmental sustainability, leadership, and community engagement. It also encouraged me to think critically about environmental challenges and how I can contribute to addressing them within my community.

One of the most valuable aspects of the programme was the class sessions, practical assignments and challenges. Activities focused on issues such as improper waste disposal, flooding, and climate action helped me understand that leadership is not just about having ideas but also about taking initiative, listening to affected communities, identifying stakeholders, and developing realistic solutions. The activities also encouraged me to communicate environmental issues more effectively and use social media to raise awareness.

I particularly appreciated the opportunity to learn from the sessions, engage with other participants, and reflect on my role as a young woman interested in environmental health and sustainability. The programme motivated me to become more intentional about my personal development and to look for practical ways to contribute to positive environmental change.

Overall, I am grateful for the opportunity to participate in the Womate She Leads Programme. It has strengthened my interest in climate leadership and environmental sustainability while reminding me that meaningful change begins with individual action and community involvement. I hope the programme continues to grow and create more opportunities for young women to develop their leadership skills, share ideas, and contribute to sustainable solutions.

I have gained valuable knowledge about climate advocacy, leadership, teamwork, and communicating climate issues in ways that encourage people to take action. The activities also challenged me to think critically, share my ideas, and explore practical solutions to the climate challenges affecting my community.

One of the most important lessons I have taken from this experience is that young people, especially young women, should not only be included in conversations about climate change but should also be empowered to lead solutions. I hope to apply what I have learned by raising awareness in my community and promoting practical approaches to climate resilience, particularly around water conservation and management.

Thank you to the She Leads team, mentors, and fellow participants for creating this learning opportunity. I would appreciate continued opportunities for mentorship, collaboration, networking, and practical community-based climate projects that allow participants to turn their knowledge into measurable impact.

The She Leads Climate Mentorship Programme has been a valuable learning experience that has helped me reflect on my leadership journey and strengthen my commitment to climate action. However, this programme has helped me appreciate climate action from a broader perspective, particularly the importance of women's leadership, community participation, and listening to people before proposing solutions to environmental challenges.
The mentorship sessions have encouraged me to think more critically about the environmental challenges affecting my community, including deforestation caused by the demand for firewood and charcoal. They have also helped me recognise that addressing these challenges requires not only awareness campaigns but also practical, affordable, and sustainable solutions that consider the realities of the people affected.
I particularly appreciated learning from the speakers and gaining new perspectives on leadership, personal growth, and climate action. The programme has helped shape my approach to leadership by encouraging me to be more intentional, inclusive, and solution-oriented in my community engagement work.
Overall, I am grateful to have been part of the programme because it has built on my existing experience with YASCON and motivated me to continue contributing to environmental conservation. I would appreciate more practical, hands-on activities, networking opportunities, and continued mentorship to help participants turn the knowledge gained into tangible community-based climate initiatives.

name: Ewa Firmine OLOU
quote:
I am Ewa Firmine OLOU, a young Beninese researcher in livestock, gender and food security from Parakou. 

My experience in Cohort 2 of the She Leads Climate Mentorship Program has been transformative.

Before WOMATE, I had the technical knowledge from my fieldwork in Tchaourou and Banikoara on agropastoral conflicts, but I lacked confidence to position myself as a climate leader. Through the modules on climate leadership, gender and climate justice, advocacy, and personal branding, I learned to connect my research to real community impact.

What I appreciated most:
- The practical exercises after each module (especially the leadership reflection and the community mapping exercise) forced me to apply concepts to my own context in Northern Benin.
- The mentorship and sisterhood: sharing with other African women facing similar challenges gave me strength.
- The safe space to practice English and to present my work on women in livestock and climate resilience.

This program helped me understand that my work on women's access to pastoral resources is not just academic, it is climate action. I am now more confident to speak, to lead community dialogues on social cohesion.

Thank you to the SHE Leads team for your honesty, support and integrity. The program is well-structured, impactful and truly needed for young women scientists like me.

I give my consent for this feedback to be used as a testimonial. You can use my name.

• Deepened Climate Literacy: The sessions provided an excellent foundation in understanding complex environmental issues, specifically how global climate change directly impacts African ecosystems, seasonal rainfall, and long-term agricultural stability.

• Eye-Opening Perspective on Climate Justice: Learning about the
 intersection of gender and climate change highlighted how rural women farmers bear a disproportionate burden of environmental shifts, making climate-resilient solutions more urgent than ever.

• Empowered for Agricultural Advocacy: The training gave me the confidence and knowledge to actively advocate for sustainable farming practices, focusing on helping local farmers adapt to unpredictable weather patterns and protect their crop yields.

From the beginning of the programme to the end, I have gained knowledge, confidence, and a better understanding of climate change, leadership, and the role I can play in my community.

At the beginning, I understood climate change mainly as an environmental issue, but through the different sessions, I learned how it affects our daily lives, our communities, livelihoods, and future generations. The programme helped me understand that climate action does not always have to start with big projects. Small actions, awareness, and working together as a community can also make a difference.

One of the most important lessons I learned was the importance of listening to people before suggesting solutions. I also learned about leadership, self-confidence, communication, and taking initiative. The mentorship sessions encouraged me to think about how I can use the knowledge I have gained to contribute positively to my community and inspire others, especially fellow young women.

I appreciate the mentors and facilitators for sharing their knowledge, guidance, and experiences throughout the programme. I am also grateful for the opportunity to learn alongside other participants, share ideas, and gain different perspectives on climates challenges and solutions.

As we come to the end of the programme, I feel more informed, motivated, and ready to take small but meaningful steps towards climate action. I understand that completing the programme is not the end of the journey, but the beginning of putting what I have learned into practice.

For future cohorts, I would encourage more practical activities, community based projects, and opportunities for participants to connect with each other and implement their ideas. Continued mentorship and follow-up support would also help participants turn their knowledge into lasting impact.

Overall, I am grateful to WOMATE for providing this learning opportunity. The programme has reminded me that leadership begins with listening, learning, and taking action, and that every one of us has a role to play in creating a more sustainable future.

Thank you, WOMATE, and thank you to all the mentors and fellow participants for being part of this journey.

name: Comfort kaphuka
quote:
Joining the She Leads Climate Mentorship Programme has been one of the most meaningful steps I’ve taken in my climate journey so far.
As a young woman who cared deeply about climate issues but often felt unsure about where to start or how to contribute meaningfully, this programme gave me both the knowledge and the confidence I needed. The modules were practical and relevant especially the sessions on understanding climate change in the African context, gender and climate justice, and climate governance and policy. I particularly appreciated how the programme didn’t just teach theory, but constantly pushed us to connect what we were learning to our own communities and experiences.
The assignments challenged me in the best way. Reflecting on my own climate justice story and reviewing national adaptation plans helped me move from simply caring about the issues to thinking critically about solutions and my role in them. I also loved the sense of community. Connecting with other young women across Africa who share the same passion made me feel less alone and more hopeful about the future of climate leadership on the continent.
Beyond the knowledge, the programme strengthened my voice. I now feel more equipped to speak up, advocate, and take action. The networking and mentorship aspects created a supportive space where I could grow without pressure, and receiving the certificate at the end felt like a meaningful recognition of that growth.
Of course, no programme is perfect. I would have loved even more one-on-one mentorship time and deeper guidance on turning ideas into concrete projects. But overall, She Leads has been a strong foundation one that has shifted how I see myself as a climate leader.
I’m truly grateful to WOMATE for creating this space for young African women. If you’re a student or recent graduate looking to move from climate concern to credible action, I would highly recommend this programme. It was exactly the step I needed.

name: Mariama Mubanatu Kamara
quote:
Being part of Cohort 2 of the She Leads Climate Mentorship Programme has been a valuable learning experience for me. The programme has strengthened my understanding of climate change, gender and climate justice, community resilience, and the importance of youth and women’s participation in climate action.

One of my biggest takeaways has been learning to connect climate issues to the realities of our communities and understanding that leadership does not always require a big platform or significant resources; it can begin with recognising a problem and taking practical steps towards addressing it. The assignments and cross-country climate mission also encouraged me to research, think critically, collaborate with other women across Africa, and consider how my background in economics and communications can contribute to climate action in Sierra Leone.

I appreciate the opportunity to learn alongside other passionate women and develop my confidence as an emerging climate advocate. For future cohorts, I would encourage continued practical activities, more opportunities for direct engagement with climate professionals, and stronger follow-up support to help participants turn their learning into community projects and measurable action. Overall, the programme has been meaningful, informative, and encouraging, and I am grateful to have been part of it.

name: Cecilia Serwaa Nkansah
quote:
The She Leads mentorship program Dear WOMATE Team,
I want to express my sincere gratitude to the entire WOMATE team for giving us this wonderful opportunity to learn, grow, and become more intentional about climate action and leadership.

This program has broadened my understanding of climate change, climate justice, and the important role women play in creating sustainable solutions within their communities. I have learned that climate action is not just about addressing environmental challenges; it is also about recognizing vulnerable communities, amplifying their voices, ensuring their participation, and empowering them to be part of the solutions.

One of my biggest takeaways is that women should not only be seen as people affected by climate change but also as leaders, innovators, advocates, and agents of change. The knowledge and skills I have gained have strengthened my confidence and inspired me to contribute more meaningfully to climate advocacy and community-based action, particularly in addressing issues such as flooding and environmental degradation in Ghana.

Thank you for creating a platform where our voices, ideas, and experiences matter. I am grateful for the lessons, the inspiration, and the opportunity to be part of this journey. Although we are graduating today, I see this as the beginning of a greater commitment to climate leadership and action.

Congratulations to the WOMATE team and all my fellow participants! May we continue to turn the knowledge we have gained into meaningful action in our communities.

Thank you, WOMATE, for being part of our growth and for empowering women to lead the change our planet needs.
